title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp. 22-24. A 'figure' F in an ambient space L is a family of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets (its 'multiplicités', or pieces) with support |F| = union of the pieces. The pieces carry a closure-type relation (notation A^0, A^*), which induces a partial order on F. Page 24 makes this explicit: a figure is the same thing as a surjective semicontinuous map p : |F| -> I onto a poset I. In modern terms a figure is a poset-stratification of a subset of L. Refinement F << G (defined p.22) means each piece of F lies in a piece of G, compatibly with closures and order; << is an order relation. Sub-figure F <= G (defined at the bottom of p.23, notation fixed p.24) means F is a subfamily of G.

Proposition (statement p.22, proof p.23). For figures F, G the following are equivalent:
(a) F << G and F is maximal (for <=) among refinements of G, i.e. any refinement F' of G with F <= F' equals F.
(b) F << G and |F| = |G|.

Proof of (b) => (a). If F' << G with F <= F', then |F| ⊂ |F'| ⊂ |G| = |F|, so |F'| = |F|. A sub-figure with the same support must equal the whole figure, so F = F'.

Proof of (a) => (b). Suppose |F| ≠ |G|. Pick x in |G| \ |F| and set H = {{x}}. Then H is nonempty, refines G, and is disjoint from F.

Corollary. If F and H refine G and are disjoint, then F ∪ H refines G. Reason: the pieces of F ∪ H are pieces of F or of H, and refinement is checked piece by piece. Hence F < F ∪ H << G, contradicting maximality.

Marginal items (c) and (d) begin further characterisations, roughly: F maximal iff ...; for all A in F there exists B in G with |B| ⊃ A and CA = C(A) ∩ |B|, i.e. relative closures agree.

Purpose. The page builds the elementary order theory ('algebra') of stratifications under refinement and sub-figure, presumably as groundwork for a combinatorial/tame-topology treatment of stratified spaces.
errors: The corollary is stated too quickly. That F ∪ H is a figure, and refines G, needs more than piecewise checking: the closure/order compatibility between pieces of F and pieces of H must also hold (e.g. closure of a piece of F meeting a piece of H). Grothendieck's own marginal note says conditions are needed ('il faut que ... soient disjointes ...'). The written argument 'refinement is checked on the multiplicities' does not cover these cross-conditions.

In (a) => (b), one must also check that the singleton {x} is a legitimate piece and that H = {{x}} refines G. This depends on the precise definition, e.g. on how the closure conditions behave relative to the piece of G containing x. The claim is plausible but not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Maximal refinements of a figure/stratification are exactly the refinements with full support
ideas.modern_name: elementary order theory of refinements of (partial) stratifications

ideas.what: Disjoint union of refinements is a refinement; refinement is checked stratum by stratum
Figure as a surjective semicontinuous map from the support onto a poset (stated on the next page, underlying this one)
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified space: continuous map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A); also Treumann; Barwick-Glasman-Haine; Haine
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tame topology and stratified structures but not, to my knowledge, this formal definition

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine order-theoretic lemma about refinements of stratification-like 'figures' plus a corollary on disjoint unions. The conceptually interesting point, a stratification as a semicontinuous map to a poset (anticipating the now-standard definition), appears on the next page, not here.
transcription_corrections: In the proof of a) => b), the transcription's '$x \in |G| \setminus |F|$' also appears as '$x \in |G| \setminus |F|$,' in the image (the image may read '|G| \ |F|' written with a G resembling '6').
The bottom definition reads 'On dit dans ce cas que F est une sous-figure de G', defining the sub-figure relation notated ≼ on p.24. 'sous-figure' is struck out and rewritten, not omitted.
Margin c) begins 'Démonstration ... c) ⇒' (rotated) and includes 'F ≪ G' (double angle) rather than '≺≺'.
